svg.title: Azure AI Observatory architecture at a glance
svg.desc: A logical Azure architecture with five numbered flows. Existing Foundry agents and applications use app-configured OpenTelemetry instrumentation and an exporter to send traces to Application Insights and Log Analytics. Evaluation events are optional. No OpenTelemetry Collector is deployed. Azure OpenAI and PTU metrics come directly from Azure Monitor. Azure Resource Graph supplies RBAC-filtered inventory and allocated capacity. Azure Managed Grafana queries these sources using its managed identity. An optional scheduled collector reads account-attributed costs from Cost Management and sends actual and amortized snapshots through a data collection endpoint and rule to the monitoring workspace. The collector is an Azure Function in the subscription that uses a user-assigned managed identity with no client secret. Azure Monitor alerts and an optional account-filtered budget notify an action group. Terraform or Bicep deploys the observability resources; existing AI accounts are not created or resized. The tenant outline is logical, not a network boundary or live resource inventory.
svg.text: Azure AI Observatory — architecture at a glance
Agent telemetry, native metrics and optional costs converge in Grafana.
CUSTOMER AZURE TENANT • LOGICAL VIEW, NOT A NETWORK BOUNDARY
AI resources can span subscriptions; cost collection queries one. The starter uses public endpoints.
Managed identity queries permitted data sources
Cost and business views require cost collection.
Entra authentication; Grafana Admin / Viewer roles
Viewer access is not a data-isolation boundary.
Scope identity access and workspace data.
Scheduled daily once enabled • pretax actual and amortized costs for selected accounts
Billing can lag; costs are not invoice totals.
Actual and amortized amounts are alternatives.
Agent rules query the monitoring workspace.
Threshold notification, not a spending cap
No automatic PTU resizing or collector-failure alert.
Deploy with Terraform or Bicep; existing AI accounts and deployments are monitored, not created or resized.
Managed identities use scoped roles. Viewer is not data isolation; the starter uses public endpoints, not private networking.
